senses.gloss:
akiñcana-bhakti
(‘devotion that does not ask for anything else’)
------------------------------------------
From the beginning two main currents of religious thought have existed in the Hindu scriptures: that of ज्ञान (knowledge) and that of भक्ति (devotion).
The schools of devotion advocate that भक्ति is the direct means to मोक्ष (liberation) and even go to the extent of stressing that it is much easier than ज्ञान.
A devotee of God can cultivate भक्ति for several reasons: to get over his troubles, to get wealth, position or pleasures of life or to realize God. It is the last category that is भक्ति in the real sense, the others being just trading in religion. A true devotee of God, called एकान्तिन्, wants Him and Him alone and nothing else. Such a devotion is designated ‘akiñcana-भक्ति,’ a devotion that does not want anything else from Him.
